title: Post-Arthroplasty Gait
note: Generated by tools/positions.py --extract from the page itself. Edit the verification, kind, signed_off_by and note fields; everything else is rewritten on the next extraction. The detector over collects on purpose: mark anything that is teaching rather than clinical direction as NOT_CLINICAL rather than deleting it.

positions.as_written: Set expectations on function and pain rather than on normal movement, because the first recovers and the second often does not.
Ask about stairs rather than level walking when assessing recovery.
State which outcome a quoted result refers to, since gait and function diverge here.
Counsel that the operation reliably relieves pain and does not restore normal mechanics, which is both honest and usually welcome.
Measure and treat quadriceps strength before surgery, since the preoperative pattern predicts the postoperative one.
Expect patient reported scores to have a ceiling that conceals residual abnormality.
Treat kinematic arguments between alignment philosophies as real and smaller than between patient variation.

Weigh the patient's age, physiology, comorbidities, knee demand, psychological state and their own ideas, concerns and expectations, because what counts as a good result here is defined by the patient rather than by the gait laboratory.
